newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher on selective buying.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi bourse closed higher on Monday on selective buying amid expectations that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) would announce fresh rules to curb short selling, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 4.19 points higher at 704.82. It closed just before SEBI announced it was setting up a panel to fix rules for short sellers in Indian stock markets.

"Heavy purchases by foreign institutional investors and domestic financial instititions forced bear operators to cover their short positions, which also had a positive impact on sentiment," Varinder Singh, of brokers Fairdeal Investments, said.
ITC closed 19.45 rupees, or seven percent, higher at 283.95 while Reliance Industries rose 4.10 rupees to 191.85.
TISCO closed three rupees higher at 171 and State Bank of India was quoted 5.65 rupees higher at 228.65.
Larsen and Toubro ended 8.55 rupees higher at 233.95.
